Subject: [PATCH] e1000: fix OOB in e1000_tbi_should_accept()

In e1000_tbi_should_accept() we read the last byte of the frame via
'data[length - 1]' to evaluate the TBI workaround. If the descriptor-
reported length is zero or larger than the actual RX buffer size, this
read goes out of bounds and can hit unrelated slab objects. The issue
is observed from the NAPI receive path (e1000_clean_rx_irq):

This happens because the TBI check unconditionally dereferences the last
byte without validating the reported length first:

	u8 last_byte = *(data + length - 1);

Fix by rejecting the frame early if the length is zero, or if it exceeds
adapter->rx_buffer_len. This preserves the TBI workaround semantics for
valid frames and prevents touching memory beyond the RX buffer.

Fixes: 2037110c96d5 ("e1000: move tbi workaround code into helper function")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Guangshuo Li <lgs201920130244@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Aleksandr Loktionov <aleksandr.loktionov@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Tony Nguyen <anthony.l.nguyen@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/e1000/e1000_main.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/e1000/e1000_main.c
index 292389aceb2d..7f078ec9c14c 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/e1000/e1000_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/e1000/e1000_main.c
@@ -4094,7 +4094,15 @@ static bool e1000_tbi_should_accept(struct e1000_adapter *adapter,
 				    u32 length, const u8 *data)
 {
 	struct e1000_hw *hw = &adapter->hw;
-	u8 last_byte = *(data + length - 1);
+	u8 last_byte;
+
+	/* Guard against OOB on data[length - 1] */
+	if (unlikely(!length))
+		return false;
+	/* Upper bound: length must not exceed rx_buffer_len */
+	if (unlikely(length > adapter->rx_buffer_len))
+		return false;
+	last_byte = *(data + length - 1);
 
 	if (TBI_ACCEPT(hw, status, errors, length, last_byte)) {
 		unsigned long irq_flags;
-- 
2.34.1

The patch addresses an out-of-bounds (OOB) read vulnerability in the `e1000_tbi_should_accept()` function of the Intel e1000 network driver. The bug occurs because the function unconditionally accesses `data[length - 1]` without validating the `length` parameter, leading to reads beyond the allocated RX buffer when `length` is zero or exceeds the buffer size. This is triggered in the NAPI receive path (`e1000_clean_rx_irq`), causing a KASAN slab-out-of-bounds report.

### Modifications (single file)

**`drivers/net/ethernet/intel/e1000/e1000_main.c`** (within `e1000_tbi_should_accept()`):
- Added a guard: if `length` is zero, return `false` immediately.
- Added an upper-bound check: if `length` exceeds `adapter->rx_buffer_len`, return `false`.
- After these checks, the original `last_byte` access—`*(data + length - 1)`—is performed safely.

### Relationship between modifications
Both changes are in the same function and serve a single purpose: prevent the out-of-bounds read that occurs when `data[length - 1]` is evaluated with an invalid `length`. The checks are sequential and independent; the first eliminates the zero-length case, the second catches oversized lengths. Together they ensure that the subsequent byte access is always within the valid buffer range, preserving the TBI workaround logic only for well-formed frames.

Here is the root cause:
The root cause is the lack of validation on the `length` parameter before it is used as an index in `data[length - 1]` inside `e1000_tbi_should_accept()`. When `length` is zero or exceeds the allocated RX buffer size (`adapter->rx_buffer_len`), the access goes out of bounds, causing a slab-out-of-bounds read.

Here is the patch:
 
 static bool e1000_tbi_should_accept(struct e1000_adapter *adapter,
 				    u8 status, u8 errors,
 				    u32 length, const u8 *data)
 {
 	struct e1000_hw *hw = &adapter->hw;
-	u8 last_byte = *(data + length - 1);
+	u8 last_byte;
+
+	/* Guard against OOB on data[length - 1] */
+	if (unlikely(!length))
+		return false;
+	/* Upper bound: length must not exceed rx_buffer_len */
+	if (unlikely(length > adapter->rx_buffer_len))
+		return false;
+	last_byte = *(data + length - 1);
 
 	if (TBI_ACCEPT(hw, status, errors, length, last_byte)) {
 		unsigned long irq_flags;
 
 		spin_lock_irqsave(&adapter->stats_lock, irq_flags);
 		e1000_tbi_adjust_stats(hw, &adapter->stats, length, data);
 		spin_unlock_irqrestore(&adapter->stats_lock, irq_flags);
 
 		return true;
 	}
 
 	return false;
 }
